Start with the question

Can we still tell how the work ended after we keep fewer records?

An answer passes only when its outcome, failure location, and evidence checks match the test rules.

Read this in three steps

  1. Choose a saved test and compare its case results.
  2. Open an answer to see the exact records behind it.
  3. Check which saved evidence restored the missing answers.

Every choice below shows a test that already ran.

What do these words mean?
Evidence
Records that can help answer a question about the work.
Outcome
Whether the work finished, failed, or was still pending.
Answer that passed
The outcome, failure location, and evidence checks matched the test rules.
Trace and span
A trace records steps in a request. A span is one recorded step.
Log
A message written by an application program.
Saved status
The application's response when it was asked about the work.
Replay
An investigation of saved records. It does not rerun or repair the application.
Restoration
Adding previously saved records back into a test.
Cause
The reason something happened. Knowing the outcome does not always establish the cause.

What changed when records were removed?

The reduced test removes outcome records from logs and saved status responses. It keeps the traces. Restoration tests add selected saved records back.

What this review does and does not establish

25 saved investigations · 5 cases · 4 scenario groups.

  • These results cover five examples created for this project. They do not predict results for other applications.
  • The separate API comparison has not run. Additional-cost API execution is disabled by the owner. Subscription investigations remain disabled. This page shows fixed-rule results.
  • The test removes or adds saved records. It does not measure application performance or a service bill.
  • This run used the Mac sandbox. The Docker access check is a separate test.
  • These saved examples use an invented test clock. The application capture checks real execution separately.

Reference checks do not verify every sentence written by an investigator. These results do not establish an accuracy rate, production safety, or financial savings.
